brief: The S&P 500 rose less than 1% from end-May to end-September 2026, and markets were flat from around mid-July to early October ahead of this week, echoing the setup before most historical midterm rallies. Per DB strategists Binky Chadha and Parag Thatte, the S&P 500 has risen in 21 of the last 23 midterm election cycles over the window from one month before the election to two months after, median return 7%, well above a normal quarterly return, and markets just entered that window. The two exceptions were 1978, when a dollar crisis (-8% in October) forced the Fed to hike 100bps to 9.5% on November 1, and 2018, when Powell called the Fed "a long way from neutral" amid a US-China trade war, with markets not recovering until Powell turned dovish in January 2019. Both exceptions had rate moves far larger and more urgent than today's, with the dollar slumping then versus rising now. Unlike either exception, Q3 earnings season starts next week with YoY growth expected above 30% (DB forecasts 34% YoY EPS growth), a tailwind DB expects to help the seasonal pattern reassert itself despite the recent rates selloff.
